summary: The tag-consuming loop in parse_user_spec halted at the first tag it could not decode, so a NOPASSWD: sitting behind SETENV:/NOEXEC: was never decoded and a genuinely passwordless root grant reported nopasswd|false with status OK and no failure token. Introduced by this branch's own earlier fix 5bcd2d3a1, which traded a silent SETENV: drop for an inverted nopasswd column. Fixed 4f4978043.
trigger: a sudoers user spec whose Tag_Spec puts another valid tag before NOPASSWD:, e.g. `%ops ALL=(root) SETENV: NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/bar` -- ordinary syntax, sudoers(5) allows tags in any order
classification_rationale: The emitted row asserts a security property (password required) that is the opposite of what the host's sudoers grants; the code contradicted the contract its own comment stated.

summary: The Tag_Spec scan was keyed on whitespace while sudo's lexer is keyed on the colon (NOPASSWD[[:blank:]]*:), so NOPASSWD:/bin/ls, NOPASSWD :/bin/ls, NOPASSWD : /bin/ls and SETENV:NOPASSWD:/bin/ls -- all accepted by visudo -- reported nopasswd|false for passwordless root grants. Distinct from sg-01, which was tag ORDER; this is tag LEXING. Fixed 9d99df056.
trigger: any sudoers user spec whose NOPASSWD tag omits the blank after its colon or carries one before it; confirmed valid by `visudo -c` on sudo 1.9.17p2
classification_rationale: Same class as sg-01 and found only because Gate 4 attacked the lexer rather than the ordering: the most security-relevant column of the row was inverted while the result claimed OK/FULL.

summary: AuditRuleCounts::total counted every non-comment line, so auditd CONTROL directives (-D, -b, -f, -e, --backlog_wait_time) were reported as rules. The committed debian:12 real capture is four control directives and ZERO rules, and reported `rules|4`; the fedora:40 capture reported `rules|7` against watch 2 + syscall 3 + unmodelled 0 = 5, so the row set did not close. `rules` is now the rule count and a new control_lines row accounts for the remainder. Fixed 9d99df056.
trigger: audit_policy on any Linux host with auditd installed and a stock rule file; reproduced directly against the committed fixture
classification_rationale: The headline row of the action answered 'four rules' for a host with no audit rules at all, at FULL completeness with no token -- a wrong answer presented as correct, and the arithmetic of the row set visibly did not close.

summary: Windows audit_policy reports the nine LEGACY [Event Audit] categories from secedit /export and presented them as the host's audit policy. Where Advanced Audit Policy subcategories are in force -- the Windows 10/11 default and the norm under GPO -- those are not the effective audit state, so a fully-audited host reads every category `none`. The branch's own rig capture is exactly that shape. Declared now in the descriptor note, the definition description and README caveat 6; reading auditpol would be a second argv leaf and its own sink-manifest row, deliberately out of scope.
trigger: dispatch audit_policy against any Windows host whose audit policy is set at the subcategory level, which is the Windows 10/11 default
classification_rationale: The hazard was not stated anywhere: the existing declarations named what was not READ (coverage), never that a `none` in what IS read does not mean the host is not auditing. The Linux leg already hedges this way at the definition level; Windows did not.

summary: The Windows scratch sweep is a wall-clock-cutoff reclaim pass, so the clock-guarded-retention routed concern applies. It took the sibling's guard constants and recorded neither the per-part adopt/decline reasoning nor a row in the routed doc's per-store adoption register. Fixed f57c4dfc2.
trigger: any local_security_policy dispatch on Windows with agent.data_dir set: is_stale gates removal on now - mtime > 3600 on every dispatch
classification_rationale: POLICY FLOOR. The routed-concerns row states in terms that what makes any of the seven parts correct is the RECORDED reasoning, not the answer, and that copying a guard without deciding IS the defect.
policy_floor: a catastrophic-if-violated clause in a .claude/routed-concerns.md row (Clock-guarded retention: 'What makes any of them correct is the RECORDED reasoning, not the answer -- copying a guard without deciding IS the defect')

summary: The adoption record written for ce-01 asserted two differences from execution_artifacts that do not exist: that this sweep adds a kScratchSweepMaxFailures cap 'the sibling does not have' (the sibling declares it at line 118, same value 256) and that kScratchSweepMaxDirEntries differs (both are 64). Those two claims were the stated evidence of independent derivation. Corrected in both the header banner and the register row, and the sibling's own stale 'four caps' corrected to five.
trigger: reading either text against agents/plugins/execution_artifacts/src/execution_artifacts_scratch_sweep.hpp:100-126
classification_rationale: Self-inflicted by the ce-01 fix and caught in the same run. The header tells a maintainer 'a fix to either copy MUST be applied to both'; a maintainer who believed the failure cap existed in only one copy would not carry a fix across -- the precise drift the two-copy warning exists to prevent.

summary: The <action>|status|<state>|<reason> fallback row added by f9fbe5acd was named in no operator-facing document: the definitions' key column listed only source_state, and the source column's documented vocabulary would have led a reader to parse `pwpolicy:deadline` as a policy identifier. Fixed e68372a7e.
trigger: macOS password_policy or lockout_policy where the pwpolicy run fails (spawn error, deadline, truncated output, non-zero exit, no plist, unparseable plist)
classification_rationale: Found independently by security-guardian and docs-writer. The definition YAML is the operator-facing data contract, rendered into the README, the plugin-docs JSON and /api/v1/discover/plugin-docs.

summary: The sudoers `subject` column was documented and exemplified as `%sudo`; parse_user_spec builds <user>@<host>, so every real user_spec row reads `%sudo@ALL`. The branch's own committed test assertions had said so all along. Fixed e68372a7e.
trigger: any sudoers user-spec row on any Linux or macOS host
classification_rationale: The published contract for the field that answers 'who may become root' did not match the emitted value.

summary: The macOS rung-2 descent cited 'ADR-3002 K10' in four places; ADR-3002 has no K-series (K10 is an adversarial-review finding-id convention). That citation was the recorded rung evidence, and ADR-3002 Decision 1 states in the same sentence that a bare assertion is not evidence. Replaced with Decision 1's real 'no interface exists' category plus the substantive claim. Fixed 2f2d44f80.
trigger: grep K10 docs/adr/3002-acquisition-ladder.md returns nothing
classification_rationale: A citation pointing at nothing reduces an ADR-mandated evidence record to the bare assertion the ADR forbids.

summary: This branch takes ServerImpl's capability registry from 15 sources to 16 against kMaxSources = 16, while the constant's doc comment still described it as 'a generous ceiling, not a tight fit, so an additional fragment group does not silently overflow it'. Comment corrected to state the live count, the mirrors that move with it and that the next fragment carries the 16->32 raise. Fixed f54fd700a, mirror list completed this round.
trigger: a 17th catalogue source added to server.cpp; CI reddens first on test_dispatch_destructive_gate.cpp's std::array<..., 16>, in a file whose name does not suggest why
classification_rationale: The in-tree contract text for the composition seam was wrong at exactly the moment it would be consulted.

summary: posix_read_file opened O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC and only then fstat'd for S_ISREG, so open(2) on a FIFO with no writer never returns and the type filter never runs -- the dispatch thread wedges for the process lifetime and the frozen-seam catch cannot recover a thread blocked in a syscall. Two in-tree readers call this flag load-bearing for the same reason. Fixed 1db7efb7b.
trigger: a FIFO, a symlink to one, or a blocking device node at any path the reader is handed (login.defs, pwquality.conf, faillock.conf, the pam.d stacks, audit.rules, audit_control, sudoers, any /etc/sudoers.d entry); symlinks are followed by design so the node need not sit under /etc
classification_rationale: The house pattern is written down twice (certificates_linux_store.hpp 'peer review F1', guardian_state_reader.cpp); this plugin was the only POSIX reader in the diff with neither O_NONBLOCK nor O_NOFOLLOW.

summary: The hand-maintained 'Agent plugins (57)' per-plugin build/availability section never learned about the plugin, though every other wiring surface did, and both sibling plugin PRs bumped theirs. Row added in alphabetical position, count 57->58, and the divider's tally prose gained a bucket for a plugin constrained on all three legs. Fixed 2f2d44f80.
trigger: reading docs/os-capability-matrix.md's Agent plugins section after this branch merges
classification_rationale: Not CI-gated (the doc gates read only the capmatrix-gen block), so it would have merged as silent drift.

summary: The case named 'classify_read_errno and select_status pin the failure contract' asserted only .token for four of seven arms, never .cls -- the field deciding denied-vs-failed and failure-vs-absent. Two mutations survived the whole suite: kReadOversized -> Absent (an oversized /etc/sudoers reporting `absent` with status OK, a failure reading as absent) and EPERM -> Failed (a refusal reporting CONSTRAINED instead of PERMISSION_DENIED). Fixed 63f539fda with .cls on every arm, the missing ELOOP arm and an end-to-end oversized case.
trigger: any edit changing the ReadClass of those arms while leaving the token text alone
classification_rationale: Evidence is two surviving mutation probes, not a code read: the regression guard the case name advertises was absent for exactly the arms carrying the security-relevant distinction.

summary: Fifteen indexed reads, front()/back() calls and optional dereferences had no REQUIRE guarding them while six sibling sites in the same file did, so a regression dropping a row aborts the agent test binary mid-run and the real defect surfaces as an opaque crash rather than a named failure. Fixed 63f539fda.
trigger: the code under test regressing to produce fewer rows than the case expects (e.g. parse_auditd_rules_count dropping the enabled row makes au[4] read past the end)
classification_rationale: A test-suite robustness gap rather than a product defect, but it degrades every future failure in this file into an unattributable crash.

summary: secedit:output_short_read -- added by this branch's own fb2ecc6be -- reached the wire as a row and a typed status but was named in no document, the only one of the six secedit read tokens missing from the README's result-status table (the source the generated plugin-docs manifest reads). Fixed 70d2c280e.
trigger: read_export obtaining fewer bytes than GetFileInformationByHandle reported
classification_rationale: Found independently by unhappy-path and consistency-auditor. Notable for the next author: the doc-gen provenance gate only harvests literals written inside a set_result_status(...) call, so a token returned from a pure classifier and passed by variable is structurally invisible to CI.

summary: format_sweep_summary summed skipped_fresh + skipped_not_ours + failed + deferred into one number, and failed and deferred have no other log line, row, token or metric -- so 'two concurrent dispatches' (healthy) and 'two orphans that cannot be removed' (disk accumulating) produced the identical string. The wire carries no provenance for a sweep, so this log line is its only health surface. Now names every counter, and only logs when a pass did something (warn, not info).
trigger: any Windows dispatch where a stale orphan cannot be reclaimed: unlink failure, missing mtime, volume/reparse mismatch, non-flat candidate, or a spent cap
classification_rationale: CommandResponse carries no provenance field, so the agent log is the only possible surface for sweep health and it was ambiguous.

summary: Every macOS capture is from an explicitly unmanaged Mac and the Windows capture from a standalone host, yet nothing stated whether an MDM configuration-profile passcode payload surfaces in pwpolicy -getaccountpolicies, or what a domain-joined member's export does contain. On a managed Mac lockout_policy|policies|none -- which the descriptor calls 'the default' -- could read as 'no lockout enforced' on a host where the MDM does enforce one. Declared now in the descriptor notes and README caveat 7.
trigger: dispatch password_policy or lockout_policy on an MDM-managed Mac, or any action on a domain-joined Windows member
classification_rationale: The modal enterprise endpoint is exactly the shape with no evidence and no declaration. Verified as an evidence-and-declaration gap; the consequence on a managed Mac is reasoned, not measured, and is called out as unverified rather than asserted either way.

summary: The same fact carries four spellings across the legs (Windows MinimumPasswordLength, Linux PASS_MIN_LEN and pwquality minlen, macOS minimum_length) and the only aggregation offered is groupBy: source, itself OS-specific, so a fleet query such as 'every host weaker than our baseline' cannot be built without per-OS branching -- and nothing said so. Declared now in both kv definitions and README caveat 8.
trigger: an operator building a fleet query over password_policy across a mixed Windows/macOS/Linux estate
classification_rationale: The finding is the UNDECLARED absence, not a missing feature: the roadmap asks for the facts, not a normalised baseline, and the source field does name the origin on every row.

summary: posix_list_dir opened a DIR* and closed it with a bare ::closedir after walk_dir_capped returned, so a throw from the callback (it appends to a vector) would leak the stream. autoruns_linux.cpp wraps the same shared primitive in a three-line DirGuard for exactly this reason. Fixed c7103fdca.
trigger: an exception between opendir and closedir, e.g. std::bad_alloc while enumerating /etc/sudoers.d
classification_rationale: POLICY FLOOR. Derived band is LOW (the throw is already contained by the frozen-seam catch and the residue is one leaked stream), but manual non-RAII cleanup in new C++ gates regardless.
policy_floor: manual (non-RAII) resource cleanup in NEW C++

summary: The zero-row fallback that implements 'never an empty result' at the WIRE level has no test on the macOS pwpolicy path, which is the only path that reaches it. The file-leg half of the invariant is now pinned (9c5292243 plus the fail-closed cases in 68beddef9), and the status/provenance half is covered by the dispatcher TU, but no test drives apply_collected itself with an empty non-OK Collected.
trigger: macOS pwpolicy failure (spawn error, deadline, exit_N, unparseable plist); not reachable on a host where pwpolicy succeeds, which is every host in CI
classification_rationale: Left open deliberately: closing it needs the run_with_ctx harness (test_execution_artifacts_win_internals.cpp's pattern) to drive a real CommandContext, which is a larger test-infrastructure change than the remaining findings justify at this point in the gate sequence. The behaviour itself is correct and was verified by static trace in Gate 2.

summary: On the modal Debian/Ubuntu host faillock.conf is present-but-comment-only (a successful read emitting no rows) and the auth stack carries no pam_faillock line, so the entire lockout_policy answer is three login.defs keys that are login(1) prompt knobs, not an account-lockout threshold, window or duration -- and there is no 'nothing configured' row equivalent to the macOS leg's policies|none.
trigger: lockout_policy on the committed debian:12 real capture
classification_rationale: DEFERRED, not rejected: the fix adds a row, which would make the committed docs/samples/linux.txt real capture stale, and this host cannot recapture the Linux sample (it is a container capture). It should ride with the next change that legitimately recaptures the Linux leg. Every row emitted today is correctly labelled with its key and source, so nothing asserts a control is in place.

summary: password_policy silently filters /etc/login.defs to seven keys and nothing declares that login.defs is filtered at all for that action. The committed fedora:40 capture contains PASS_CHANGE_TRIES and PASS_ALWAYS_WARN, both dropped; the list also keeps SHA_CRYPT_MIN/MAX_ROUNDS while omitting YESCRYPT_COST_FACTOR, though both captures and the live sample report ENCRYPT_METHOD YESCRYPT.
trigger: password_policy on a host whose login.defs carries a password-relevant key outside the seven-key allowlist
classification_rationale: DEFERRED for the same reason as hp-02: adding keys changes what a Linux capture emits and would make the committed sample stale, unrecapturable from this host. The declaration half could land alone, but splitting the fix would leave the doc describing a key set the next change is about to alter.

summary: kSeceditLockoutKeys omits AllowAdministratorLockout (Windows 11 22H2+, on by default) and kSeceditPasswordKeys omits MinimumPasswordLengthAudit; a key absent from the allowlist is not even reported `absent`, unlike an allowlisted key the export does not carry.
trigger: lockout_policy on a stock Windows 11 22H2+ host; not provable from the committed rig export, whose LockoutBadCount is 0 so the dependent keys are not written at all
classification_rationale: DEFERRED. Epistemic status is the weakest of the Gate 4 set -- reasoned from the Windows policy surface, not from any committed byte, and the reporter said so. Adding keys also adds `absent` rows to what a Windows capture emits, and the Windows sample cannot be recaptured from this host. Wants a rig session to confirm the key names and defaults before it is worth doing.

summary: ~ScratchDirGuard wraps its spdlog::warn in try/catch but not the two statements above it; std::filesystem::path{path_} and remove_all(..., ec) can throw bad_alloc (the error_code overload suppresses filesystem_error, not allocation failure), and a destructor is implicitly noexcept, so that is std::terminate.
trigger: heap exhaustion during the guard's destruction, including during a stack unwind that execute()'s catch would otherwise contain
classification_rationale: OPEN by deliberate adjudication: agents/plugins/execution_artifacts/src/execution_artifacts_win.cpp:344-346 is byte-for-byte the same shape with the same rationale, already in-tree and accepted, and both Gate 3 and Gate 4 reporters said to fix both or neither. Fixing only this copy would create exactly the divergence between the two copies that the scratch-sweep header warns against. Belongs with the agents/core extraction (ce-05).

summary: The Windows sudoers leg declares {UNSUPPORTED, 0, "no sudoers on Windows", nullptr}, putting the reason in the MECHANISM field and leaving the limitation note null. It is the only one of 56 unsupported legs in the tree shaped that way; every sibling writes {…, 0, nullptr, "<reason>"}. The visible cost is one missing bullet in the README's generated 'Declared limits per leg' list.
trigger: rendering any generated artifact for this leg; no runtime input required
classification_rationale: The reporters labelled this LOW; the facts derive MEDIUM (I7 base MEDIUM, E0 no change, E7 caps at MEDIUM), and the derived band governs -- recorded as native LOW, mapped SHOULD. DEFERRED after being attempted and reverted. leg_hash() hashes support, rung and MECHANISM and explicitly excludes fallback, so moving the string invalidates the capture stamps for ALL THREE OS samples and demands a recapture. This host cannot recapture Windows or Linux, and re-stamping without recapturing would defeat a deliberate tripwire -- and would re-stamp the macOS and Linux captures for a Windows-only descriptor change. Should ride with the next change that legitimately recaptures all three legs.

summary: The sudoers action returns a host's full privilege-escalation map -- subject, run-as, NOPASSWD flag and command allowlist -- and is published as RiskTier::Low, while antivirus.av_exclusions is Medium on reasoning ('a map of where AV coverage has gaps') that applies here with more force. Two independent Gate reviewers (architect, compliance-officer) recommend Medium for sudoers alone, leaving the other three actions at Low.
trigger: any reader of the published plugin doc or the MCP yuzu://plugin-docs resource comparing this row against plugin_action_catalogue_d.hpp:480
classification_rationale: OPEN and ESCALATED rather than decided. No production code reads risk_tier (grep: only plugin_doc_gen and test assertions), and min_risk_tier_for(Read) is Low, so Low is valid rather than invalid and nothing is under-gated today. The honest counter-argument is that the nearest data analogue, users.local_admins, is also Low. Changing a published security classification across a plugin family is a judgement call for the author, not an orchestrator default.
